decisions.reason: Turnaround management software sits close to the core offer, has its own website page signalling visible public commitment, and is central to the announced data-driven airport direction, so dropping it would write off investment and expose the earlier decision.

The connectivity module builds on the established apron offer and supports the integration strategy, but it is only mentioned on the website, so commitment is moderate and it could be folded into other modules.

Billing and revenue software is further from the core operational focus and only mentioned, which makes it a more likely drop candidate, though early results after one year can still be attributed to temporary ramp-up causes.
Equipment monitoring software leverages the installed hardware base and fits the announced service and analytics expansion, so the firm is likely to persist with it.
The resource management module is close to the established offer and integral to end-to-end apron operations, so dropping it would contradict the stated direction.
The controller safety alert service supports the tower and safety positioning that the firm has publicly embraced, and safety-related investments tend to be kept despite slow uptake.
